title: Patch: show the keyboard shortcuts the client already has
thread:
**Issue #2126 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #2126: Patch: show the keyboard shortcuts the client already has
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

Part of #2036. This is a patch of its own: it goes live when it merges and builds on `main` beside the tracker's other parts.

Blocked by #2118: the hints include the command menu's own shortcut and its entries.

## What

The client already has shortcuts the player can't see: `I` to inspect (`INSPECT_KEY_SHORTCUT`), Escape on dialogs, Enter/Space on cards, and Ctrl/Cmd+K for the command menu (#2118).

- **One `Kbd` component** draws a key, showing ⌘ on Apple devices and Ctrl elsewhere.
- **Tooltips.** A control with a shortcut shows it in its tooltip.
- **The command menu.** Each entry shows its shortcut, and one place on the menu screens says that Ctrl/Cmd+K opens the menu.
- **`aria-keyshortcuts`** goes on every control with a shortcut that lacks it.
- **Touch-only devices** (`(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)`) show no hints.
- **No new hotkeys**, and above all none on the board: an End-turn key is how turns get ended by accident.

## Done when

vitest checks that:
- the inspect control's tooltip shows `I`, with ⌘ or Ctrl chosen by platform where a modifier is shown;
- command menu entries show their shortcuts;
- every control with a shortcut has `aria-keyshortcuts`;
- hints are hidden under a touch-only media query;
- no new key handler is added on board routes.

## Ground rules (from #2036)

- Read `apps/web/README.md` before changing the client. CLAUDE.md rule 7: nothing here predicts, enforces or reveals game state.
- Every number is a named constant (rule 9).
- If SPEC §10 doesn't already decide a behaviour, add a ruling note numbered from this issue's own block (`docs/issues-and-patches.md`, Ruling numbers), with its proving test named after it.
- Gates: `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test`, `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e`.
- The PR closes this issue, says `Part of #2036`, and carries one `## Player note` line.
```
